findings.title: Lightness value changed for light theme in .topic-meta-data h5 a color
findings.body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. The PR's intent is to only add a dark-theme fallback via `dark-light-choose`, preserving the existing light-theme value as the first argument. Here the first argument was changed from 30% to 70% (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`), so the light theme's rendered color for this link changes unintentionally (much lighter/washed-out), while 30% ended up assigned to the dark-theme branch instead. This is a visual regression for light theme users, inconsistent with every other conversion in this PR which keeps the original lightness value as the primary-theme argument.

findings.title: Lightness value changed for light theme in .group-member-info .name color
findings.body: Original rule: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. After conversion it became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme lightness from 30% to 50%. This alters the appearance for existing light-theme deployments instead of simply adding a dark-theme-safe fallback, unlike the sibling `.title` rule a few lines below which correctly preserves 50%->50%/50%. The 30% value appears to have been dropped/lost during the refactor.

findings.title: Lightness value changed for light theme in .group-member-info .name color (mobile)
findings.body: Same issue as the desktop counterpart: original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%, an unintended visual change rather than a pure dark-theme-compatibility fix.

findings.title: Lightness value changed for light theme in .topic-map h3 color
findings.body: Original rule: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);`. After the change it became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, i.e. the light-theme lightness moved from 20% to 50%. This is inconsistent with the rest of the PR's pattern (which keeps A and uses 100-A for the dark branch) and visibly changes heading color in light theme.

findings.title: Lightness value swapped between light/dark branches in .custom-message-length color
findings.body: Original rule: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);`. It was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The 70% value, which should remain the light-theme (first) argument per the pattern used throughout this PR, was instead moved to the dark-theme (second) argument, and 30% was substituted for light theme. This changes the light-theme appearance of this element unintentionally.
